title.narrative: QUALITAN: Quality standards and compliance programme for the United Republic of Tanzania

description.narrative: The project intervention will focus on strengthening the capacity of the Tanzania Bureau of Standards, including the functioning and reach of laboratories, standardization activities, ICT and management of information systems. Support will be provided to MSMEs to comply with standards. The action will facilitate MSME to access to compliance testing, reducing compliance costs whether in monetary terms or time delays, and facilitate market accessibility and cross-border trade. Ultimately, the intervention will also contribute to a better synchronisation of various elements of the Quality Infrastructure.

title.narrative: % reduction of costs of compliance

description.narrative: There are concerns that significant costs are imposed on businesses, and especially small and mediumsized enterprises (SMEs), due to compliance in traderelated with quality regulations and standards in Tanzania. In turn, these costs can act to erode the competitive and economic performance of businesses that import raw materials and other inputs and/or export products. These costs can take the form of testing costs, storage and other costs associated with delays, etc.There is a need to quantify the costs imposed on businesses due to traderelated safety and quality regulations and standards, both to define the scale of the problem and to demonstrate the importance of this issue to policymakers. Further, to identify which elements of these compliance processes impose the greatest costs to businesses and which might be most amenable to reform. Options might include:Turnaround time associated with the assessment and confirmation of conformity of imports and/or exports.Administrative procedures associated with the issuance of confirmation of conformity and the TBS standards mark.The cost of compliance study will determine baseline and target.

comment.narrative: The KAP survey will define a specific target based on the baseline study.
To be determined once the ongoing baseline study is completed

description.narrative: There are concerns that significant costs are imposed on businesses, and especially small and mediumsized enterprises (SMEs), due to compliance in traderelated with quality regulations and standards in Tanzania. In turn, these costs can act to erode the competitive and economic performance of businesses that import raw materials and other inputs and/or export products. These costs can take the form of testing costs, storage and other costs associated with delays, etc.There is a need to quantify the costs imposed on businesses due to traderelated safety and quality regulations and standards, both to define the scale of the problem and to demonstrate the importance of this issue to policymakers. Further, to identify which elements of these compliance processes impose the greatest costs to businesses and which might be most amenable to reform. Options might include:Turnaround time associated with the assessment and confirmation of conformity of imports and/or exports.Administrative procedures associated with the issuance of confirmation of conformity and the TBS standards mark.The cost of compliance study will determine baseline and target.

comment.narrative: The KAP survey will define a specific target based on the baseline study.
